reason: Schedule and feasibility lens. The clock does not decide this; the gate does. If the gate passed, a probe could be scored by Sat 26 about 21:00 to Sun 27 about 16:00 UTC, leaving about 2 days of slack. But the idea goes to the LB only through a correlation gate that it rates at P~0.2 itself, and the evidence says lower. So P(scored probe before 29 Sep 10:00 UTC) is about 0.08-0.17, well below 0.70. (1) The cited numbers check out. out_full_P/report.txt emb rows: 'none' z bias 44b6 +0.177 and 6bba +0.824 um; public head +0.131 and +0.447 um; the 6bba-trained head gives -0.536 um bias on 44b6 (its all-peak shift is +0.567 z; bias = gt - pred). Per-video 6bba -0.2..+1.6 um and the +1-slice median come from wf_ideas_v2/r1_research_polyphase-shift-stitch-localisation.notes.md l.4. The -0.0031 constant-offset loss is in browser_research_2026-09-24.md l.94. report.json holds no per-video bias, so the gate has to be computed from scratch. (2) The mechanism probably leaves no trace in the image, so the gate probably fails. GT coordinates are INTEGER voxels on both embryos (polyphase notes l.3). The 6bba bias, +0.824 um = 0.507 z-slices, is almost exactly half a slice. That is the fingerprint of a rounding convention (ceil vs round, or a +1 slice click habit), not of a PSF effect, and an image statistic cannot predict it. Also, a half-max intensity-centroid refinement already made localisation WORSE (<4 um 0.900 -> 0.857, r1_hyp_detection.notes.md l.12). And a per-video GT-ORACLE mean shift gave no match gain (0.9843 -> 0.9831-0.9835, l.13). So the ship rule '>= +0.001 on both embryos' very likely fails too, even when the correlation passes. My estimate is P(corr gate) about 0.1-0.15 and P(corr AND lab gain) about 0.05. (3) An LB probe cannot read the answer. The realistic effect is <= +0.0005 (sibling value verdict) against about 0.003 LB noise, so the idea's 'truth directly readable from one LB probe' claim is false. A scored probe would only check for crashes and harm. (4) Implementation as described has a runtime trap. It reads the raw image again at FINAL node positions at the output stage, for about 130 hidden videos. x138 has a 27,000 s runtime guard (h_ensembles-and-private.json): past it, relink, gap close, safe divisions and linefit switch off for the remaining datasets. A second zarr pass (roughly 20-60 s per video, guess) adds about 45-130 min, can push the last datasets past the guard, and costs about 0.025 per affected movie on private. (5) Logistics are fine and less constrained than the brief assumes. report.json args show that the USER's Windows PC (C:\Users\vital\...\train, experiments/coordhead_retrain/captures) holds the train zarr, the geffs and all 199 capture npz. The gate does not need friend A. The honest official-metric validation on x138 tails does need friend A's lab cache (availability uncertain) or a proxy on the user's PC. After the 26 Sep 00:00 UTC reset, GPU quota is not binding (40 min T4 dummy run).
fix_if_any: Make it cheap and fail-fast, and keep it off the LB unless it passes. (a) Stage 0, image-free, 10 min on the user's PC from the capture npz plus geffs: per embryo, histogram (GT z - raw peak z) in slices. If 6bba is the 44b6 distribution with about half of the nodes moved up by exactly one slice (a rounding or click convention), stop: no image statistic can predict it. (b) Stage 1, only if (a) does not show a convention: GT-oracle per-video z shift on the official metric over the x138 tails (friend A lab cache) or the raw-base 70-video proxy (zs70-style). Stop if < +0.001 on either embryo. (c) Stage 2: the image-statistic gate with Spearman >= 0.8 (not 0.5; at 0.5 the estimator noise, sd about 0.5 um, exceeds the 0.45 um residual it removes). (d) Implementation: compute the statistic at the RAW peaks inside the detection stage, where x138 already holds the frames. Carry the per-video mean forward and apply k x stat to the final float z at the writer. This adds no second zarr pass and does not move work past the 27,000 s guard. Assert that node and edge counts are identical to the base. (e) Treat any probe as a no-harm check (score >= base - 0.003), never as evidence of gain. Better still, fold the statistic into coordhead-v2 as a per-video feature, as the value verdict suggests.
realistic_public_gain: ~0 (range -0.001..+0.0005). The public embryo is probably 44b6-like: Canh's constant offset lost 0.0031. Any gain is below the 0.003 LB noise.
realistic_private_gain: ~0 (range -0.001..+0.0005). If the output-stage re-read pushes datasets past x138's 27,000 s guard, the implementation as described can LOSE about 0.005-0.02 on private.
critical_path: Owners: agent (this container, no data), the user (Windows PC with train zarr/geff plus 199 capture npz, per out_full_P report.json args; the only submitter), friend A (x138-tail lab cache, availability uncertain). Fri 25 11:30-14:30 UTC: agent writes zconv_gate.py (stage 0 histogram, stage 1 oracle, stage 2 image statistic via train_coordhead pairing, public head applied to capture features) and tests it on synthetic volumes. Fri 25 17:00-20:00: the user is busy reading #34/#35. Realistic gate run on the user's PC CPU Sat 26 06:00-09:00 (stage 0 10 min, stage 2 about 1.5-3 h over 199 videos, or 40 videos in under 1 h). Stage-1 official-metric oracle on x138 tails: friend A Sat 26 about 08:00-10:00, if available. Decision Sat 26 about 10:00. On a pass: agent builds the patch on the base picked by #34/#35 (exp56 or exp57b), with the statistic computed in the detection stage, the writer shift, and asserts, Sat 10:00-12:00. The user pushes the private kernel, T4 dummy run on 4 clips 30-40 min (quota reset at 26 Sep 00:00), Sat 12:00-13:00. The user submits about Sat 13:00; scored about Sat 20:00-23:00 UTC (7-10 h). Slack to 29 Sep 10:00: about 2.5 days, so the clock is not binding. Probability: P(stage 0 does not show a convention) about 0.4 x P(oracle >= +0.001 on both embryos) about 0.3 x P(Spearman gate) about 0.6 x P(logistics) about 0.9, giving about 0.06. Even on the idea's own P(gate)=0.2, P(scored probe) is about 0.17 < 0.70. On a gate failure there is no probe by design.
